doc.title: Allan Vaché interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000

title: Father's record collection and rebelling with Parker and Miles
summary: His father's swing and Dixieland records, and the brothers rebelling by buying Miles Davis and Charlie Parker.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well again, my dad had a humungous record collection that we listened to constantly and I heard anything from the swing era bands to early Dixieland bands and Eddie Condon style. And actually it was very funny because when my brother and I went through our adolescent rebellion in our early pre-teens and teens, our rebellion against our father was buying Miles Davis records and Charlie Parker records, which he didn’t care for because that was the music that they ruined after he came back from World War II.
I see. Look what they’ve done to my song, right? That’s funny. You know most teenagers, their rebellion is Steppenwolf or something.
Exactly. That’s what all my friends, that’s what they listened to, you know, and their parents hated it. I was listening to Charlie Parker records and my father hated it.
But you eventually — correct me if I’m wrong, please — but your tastes maybe worked backwards again?
